main_body: Timber-framed tavern: a large terracotta tile roof slope over a cream plaster wall with timber beams, shuttered windows, a plank door and a hanging sign, on a stone plinth
top_band: Roof slope, rows 0-42 at the middle column: ridge highlight rows 1-2, then scalloped orange tile courses (L 104-188) down to the eave at row ~42. It is a large horizontal-ish slope seen from above, clearly lighter and separate from the plaster wall below.
evidence: The roof reads as a tiled top slope with scalloped courses and a ridge cap, like the Beodeul house roofs. Below it, a dark eave line (row ~43) shades the plaster wall. The wall is a vertical south face with timber framing, windows with sills and shutters, and a door set in a dark frame with a lintel. No receding side faces. Both a top surface and a front face are clearly drawn, so it passes.

style.evidence: The roof tiles have 5 or so tones with per-tile highlights, and the tile-level colour count (15) is between the two references (18 and 11). Against that, 73% of the dark edge pixels are neutral, against 7-9% for the references. The roof silhouette and the wall sides carry a near-black sticker outline instead of a tinted material tone. Flat-fill coverage is 9% where the references have 0%, from the plain cream plaster panels with only sparse speckle. Total distinct colours (47) are far below the references (66 and 185). Overall it is thinner and flatter than the references, with a sticker-like outline.
